bio.description:
A short biography that can include markdown.
Supports bulleted lists, links, and inline emphasis.
Keep it concise—typically under 500 characters.
Applications may render this field with rich text.
Remember to sanitize input for security.
Empty value is allowed.

profileImageUrl.description:
Fully‑qualified URL pointing to the user’s avatar image.
The image **should** be square and ≤ 2 MB.
JPEG, PNG, and WebP formats are recommended.
Clients may cache this resource with ETag/Last‑Modified.
If not provided, a default placeholder MAY be shown.
Field can be updated independently of other data.

website.description:
Personal or company homepage address supplied by the user.
The value MUST start with `http://` or `https://`.
Applications may display this as a clickable link.
Avoid automatically embedding untrusted content.
Validation SHOULD trim surrounding whitespace.
Leaving this blank is perfectly acceptable.

metrics.description:
Aggregated usage and performance data collected by the application.
Includes counts such as page views, session length, and feature usage.
Values are typically updated by analytics pipelines.
All numbers are integers or ISO‑8601 timestamps as strings.
These metrics fuel dashboards and reports.
The object may be empty for new accounts.

permissions.description:
Role‑based access controls granted to the user.
`role` defines coarse privileges (e.g. `admin`, `viewer`).
`allowedActions` refines specific endpoints or UI features.
Clients MUST treat this as authoritative for authorization.
Changes take effect immediately after token refresh.
Ensure fine‑grained scopes are regularly reviewed.

socialLinks.description:
Collection of publicly visible profile URLs.
Keys SHOULD be well‑known platform names in lower‑case.
Values MUST be fully‑qualified URLs controlled by the user.
Clients may render icons based on the key set.
Add or remove items freely; unknown keys are ignored.
Leaving all links blank is allowed.
